key_insight: Decoupled Diffusion Inverse Solver (DDIS) separates the generative prior and the forward physics: an unconditional diffusion models the coefficient prior in function space, while a neural operator explicitly provides PDE-based guidance during sampling. This yields a data-efficient, physics-aware posterior sampler for inverse PDE problems.
problem_solved: Reduces the need for large paired coefficient–solution datasets in inverse PDE problems by avoiding joint coefficient-solution modeling and making physics explicit during sampling, enabling accurate posterior sampling with far less supervised data.
method: Train an unconditional diffusion model in function space to learn the prior over PDE coefficients (no paired solution data required).
Train or use a neural operator to model the forward PDE map; use it to provide physics-based guidance (likelihood) during diffusion sampling.
Decouple prior learning from forward physics so the sampler produces physics-consistent posterior samples with improved data efficiency and modularity.
impact: Provides practitioners a modular, scalable approach to solve inverse PDEs with fewer paired examples while respecting physical constraints—useful for scientific ML, engineering inverse design, and uncertainty quantification in high-dimensional/function-space settings.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two-module layout showing (A) unconditional diffusion prior in function space and (B) neural operator forward model feeding guidance into sampling.
Pipeline flow: coefficient prior → guided diffusion sampling → posterior samples passed through PDE forward operator to show consistency with observations.
Comparison chart: sample quality or reconstruction error vs number of paired training samples, highlighting data efficiency over joint modeling baselines.
Icon set: PDE/equation symbol, diffusion/generative model, neural operator/network, and uncertainty/posterior cloud to convey core concepts at a glance.
paper_title: Decoupled Diffusion Sampling for Inverse Problems on Function Spaces
paper_authors: Thomas Y. L. Lin, Jiachen Yao, Lufang Chiang, Julius Berner, Anima Anandkumar
